title: Why a startup founder's time is worth $1000/hour, and how it should change your decisions
summary: Jason Cohen argues founders should value their time at roughly $1000/hr, not their consultant rate. Working for a startup is like a client paying in four years with a high chance of never paying. That price forces focus, delegation, and spending money to save time.

principles.text: A founder's time is worth about $1000/hour, far above any consultant hourly rate.
principles.quote: Your time is worth $1000/hour, and you need to act accordingly.

principles.text: Founding a startup means accepting deferred, high-risk payment, so the hourly value must be priced up for that risk.
principles.quote: this isn't hypothetical, this is *exactly* the terms you're accepting for yourself when you create a startup.

principles.text: Dividing your rate by the survival odds only breaks even; you need a much larger premium to justify the risk.
principles.quote: But in fact, you need to charge far more! This formula merely brings you back to break-even!

principles.text: Skip projects that can only deliver small incremental results; focus on a few things that really matter.
principles.quote: It means you don't have time for projects that have the potential only for small, incremental results.

principles.text: Delegate far more than feels natural and spend money to buy back time (assistants, bookkeepers, CPAs, help at home).
principles.quote: It means you should delegate far more than you think.

principles.text: Stay where your maximum excellence overlaps with what is most important.
principles.quote: you need to stay in the intersection of [your zone of maximum excellence] and [the zone of importance].
